statement: Show that $\dfrac{1}{r(r+1)}=\dfrac1r-\dfrac{1}{r+1}$, and hence find $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{n}\dfrac{1}{r(r+1)}$. Deduce the limit as $n\to\infty$.
solution: The identity is a standard partial fraction. Summing from $r=1$ to $n$ gives a telescoping sum: $\sum_{r=1}^{n}\bigl(\tfrac1r-\tfrac{1}{r+1}\bigr)=1-\tfrac{1}{n+1}=\tfrac{n}{n+1}$. As $n\to\infty$, this tends to $1$.
hints: Write out a few terms to see the cancellation.
Take the limit as n tends to infinity.
